distinguishing_features: Compliant low-modulus polyurethane elastomer coating (modulus < 10 MPa, 2-5 mm) applied to the impeller surface as a passive wear barrier
Relies on extending particle-surface contact time from microseconds to milliseconds to reduce peak contact stress below the erosion/yield threshold
Strain-rate-dependent viscoelastic damping decouples impact velocity from surface stress rather than altering mass/geometry or monitoring
Uses existing flow/pressure telemetry only to detect delamination via pressure drop, not as a physics-based erosion predictor
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce erosive material removal on a slurry pump impeller surface caused by high-velocity hard quartz particle impacts without modifying impeller hardware mass or geometry and without adding new sensors.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated 1000x contact-time increase and 3-order peak-stress drop are physically overstated (impulse over a soft layer is not simply m*v/t, and elastomers still erode under hard quartz), and the 1000-hour 5% pressure-drop test is a weak proxy unconvincing for validating erosion mitigation as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying a compliant elastomer coating to absorb impact energy is a distinct passive wear-barrier mechanism not taught by any of the monitoring, duty-point, or envelope-restriction prior arts.
